description: General-purpose default for a single DGX Spark: broad tool use, long context, the safe fallback when no specialised recipe fits.
author: Alibaba Qwen Team
notes: Fills most of a 128 GB GB10 box — plan for solo operation, nothing else fits alongside. model_identifier is the served name from the recipe, not a Hugging Face repo; confirm with GET /v1/models after the first start.

description: Best single-Spark coding model to date — 78.5 % on SWE-bench Multilingual. First choice for agent work on one GB10 box.
author: poolside
notes: Weights ~71 GB; the min_vram figure adds KV-cache headroom for the full 256k context — shorter contexts need less. model_identifier is the served name from the recipe.

description: Sparse MoE coder (80B total, ~3B active) quantised for GB10. Fast for its size because only a fraction of the parameters run per token.
author: saricles (quant) · Alibaba Qwen Team (model)
notes: Community quant — verify quality and stability before production use. Not yet validated on a GB10 by us; the size estimate comes from the repo, not from a measured run.

description: Large reasoning/general model, FP8. The heavyweight alternative when one box may be dedicated to a single strong model.
author: DeepSeek
notes: Solo only — nothing else fits on the box next to it. model_identifier is the served name from the recipe, not a Hugging Face repo. No launch template on file: the entry stays listed, but the switcher reports it as not startable until a registry or an operator supplies the command.

description: Mid-size all-rounder that fits comfortably on a 24 GB consumer card as well as on a Spark — the entry point for a second, smaller box.
author: Google DeepMind
notes: NVFP4 needs a Blackwell-class GPU; on older cards use an AWQ/GPTQ build of the same model instead. Size estimated from the parameter count at 4 bit, not measured.

description: The small sibling of the Spark general model — same family and prompt behaviour, small enough for a single mid-range GPU.
author: Unsloth (quant) · Alibaba Qwen Team (model)
notes: NVFP4 needs a Blackwell-class GPU. Full 256k context costs far more than the 24 GB minimum — that figure assumes a short context.

description: Small embedding model for local RAG and memory search. Runs on CPU if no GPU is free.
author: Alibaba Qwen Team
notes: Embedding models are not chat models — this serves /v1/embeddings, not /v1/chat/completions.

description: Small, fast chat model for classification, routing and drafts where a large model would be a waste of a GPU.
author: Alibaba Qwen Team
notes: Q4 quantisation trades accuracy for size — fine for routing and drafts, not for the final answer in a coding loop.

description: DeepSeek V4 Flash on the DwarfStar 4 engine (ds4-server, C/CUDA) instead of vLLM. Installs itself on a DGX Spark and serves the usual OpenAI /v1 API on port 8888.
author: MiaAI-Lab (engine: DwarfStar 4 by Salvatore Sanfilippo)
install_template: mkdir -p {src_dir} && if [ -d {src_dir}/DeepSeek-v4-Flash-One-DGX-Spark/.git ]; then git -C {src_dir}/DeepSeek-v4-Flash-One-DGX-Spark pull --ff-only; else git clone https://github.com/MiaAI-Lab/DeepSeek-v4-Flash-One-DGX-Spark {src_dir}/DeepSeek-v4-Flash-One-DGX-Spark; fi && cd {src_dir}/DeepSeek-v4-Flash-One-DGX-Spark && chmod +x start.sh stop.sh && PORT={port} CTX={ctx} DS4_GGUF_DIR={gguf_dir} ./start.sh
notes: NOT validated on a GB10 by us — gb10_validated stays false until we have watched it run. The GGUF is asymmetric: ONLY ds4-server can read these weights, vLLM cannot, which is why this ships its own server instead of a recipe. The first install pulls ~110 GiB and builds a pinned CUDA fork; that takes hours and occupies the box alone. Start is idempotent — if something already answers on the port, start.sh does nothing. Port 8888, health GET /v1/models, engine log ~/ds4-server.log. start.sh defaults CTX to 1000000 (~1M tokens); MC passes 262144 deliberately, as KV cache costs ~9.5 KiB/token. Where the weights come from is decided by the upstream installer (Entrpi/ds4-on-spark), not by MC.

description: DeepSeek V4 Flash as a pinned docker-compose stack: EXL3 weights, SparkInfer/vLLM fork, 262K context, OpenAI API on port 8000. The alternative reading of the same model to the ds4 entry — same weights family, different engine.
author: 0xSero + Local Inference Lab (SparkInfer)
stop_template: cd {src_dir}/deepseek-v4-flash-0731-spark-sparkinfer && { TUNING=""; [ -f compose.tuning.yaml ] && TUNING="-f compose.tuning.yaml"; ARGS="-f compose.yaml $TUNING -f compose.override.yaml"; docker compose $ARGS stop; }
notes: GB10-validiert am 08.08.2026: der Stack lief auf Marks DGX Spark und lieferte 18.7 tok/s Decode-Median — allerdings erst nach zwei Eingriffen, die MC seit PR 8 selbst macht. (1) Speicher: vLLM misst beim Start MemFree aus CUDA-Sicht, und davon gehen Page-Cache (nach dem 107-GB-Gewichte-Download randvoll) und vm.min_free_kbytes ab. MC leert deshalb vor dem Start den Page-Cache, haelt waehrend der Ladephase einen Cache-Dropper am Laufen und senkt — wenn die Runtime prestart_watermark_kb gesetzt hat (auf Marks Box 2097152) — das Watermark voruebergehend; danach wird exakt der vorgefundene Wert wiederhergestellt (services/host_memory_prep). (2) Tuning: die vier Werte in `env` sind das, was vorher als handgeschriebene compose.tuning.yaml auf der Box lag. MC rendert sie in den environment-Block der compose.override.yaml; eine vorhandene compose.tuning.yaml wird weiterhin zusaetzlich geladen (vor dem Override), geht also nicht verloren. Compose-Stack, kein `docker run`: der Override setzt container_name mc-<slug> und das Label mc.runtime.slug=<slug> — genau das, worueber Stop, Restart, die Start-Verifikation und die Exklusivitaets-Raeumung den Container finden. Er wird bei jedem Launch neu geschrieben, ein Re-Clone kann die Runtime also nicht verwaisen lassen. Port 8000 ist fix und NICHT konfigurierbar: das Upstream-Compose nutzt network_mode: host ohne Port-Mapping. Nur GB10/SM121 und Linux aarch64 — auf jeder anderen Box beendet sich das Image absichtlich. Der Install laedt die ~107 GB Gewichte INNERHALB des Containers beim ersten Start (danach coalesce + Draft-Build), deshalb wartet der Install-Job bis zu 4 h auf /health; spaetere Starts sind schnell. Der KV-Cache ist ein 584-Byte-gepaddeter FP8-Sparse-MLA-Record unter dem nvfp4_ds_mla-Pfad — der Repo-Titel sagt NVFP4, der Record ist FP8. Dynamische Draft-Tiefe (K1-K5) ist upstream deaktiviert (Grammar-Mask-Assertion bei strikten JSON-Schema-Requests), publiziertes Profil ist festes K5; ein dspark-Draft-Lauf ist jetzt, wo die Watermark-Automatik den Speicher freiraeumt, der naechste Versuch. HF_TOKEN wird aus der Umgebung gelesen, falls die Gewichte je gated werden. Direkter Vergleichskandidat zu deepseek-v4-flash-ds4 (gleiches Modell, DwarfStar-4-Engine, Port 8888).

description: NON-COMMERCIAL USE ONLY with the default drafter (incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0). GLM-5.3 Flash with TensorFold across two DGX Sparks (tensor parallel over RoCE): 1M-token window, 4 requests at once, OpenAI /v1 API on port 8000. Installs itself on both boxes.
author: MiaAI-Lab (engine: TensorFold by ashhart)
install_template:
(
set -euo pipefail
D={src_dir}/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-2x-DGX-Sparks-TensorFold
REV=549fdc562c477d477244d2df0590d6c14bda4889
mkdir -p "$D" && cd "$D"
[ -d .git ] || git init -q
git remote get-url origin >/dev/null 2>&1 || git remote add origin https://github.com/MiaAI-Lab/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-2x-DGX-Sparks-TensorFold
git fetch -q --depth 1 origin "$REV"
git checkout -q --detach "$REV"
echo "[mc] recipe at $REV"
source scripts/config.sh
source scripts/nodes.sh
[ "$WORKER" = "{worker_ssh}" ] || die "WORKER is '$WORKER' but MC chose '{worker_ssh}': scripts/local.sh or the environment overrides MC's .env - remove WORKER there"
[ "$TP" = 2 ] || die "TP is '$TP' but MC runs this recipe on two Sparks: scripts/local.sh or the environment sets TP - remove it there"
declare -F image_ident worker_image_ident >/dev/null || die "scripts/nodes.sh has no image_ident/worker_image_ident: upstream changed shape"
need_worker 1
REF=$(prebuilt_image)
case "$REF" in *@sha256:*) ;; *) die "no pinned image digest for these patches ($REF)" ;; esac
DIG=${REF##*@}
echo "[mc] pulling $REF on both Sparks (~37 GB each)"
docker pull -q "$REF"
worker 1 docker pull -q "$REF"
HERE=$(docker image inspect -f '{{.RepoDigests}}' "$REF")
THERE=$(worker 1 docker image inspect -f '{{.RepoDigests}}' "$REF")
case "$HERE" in *"@$DIG"*) ;; *) die "head: $REF has RepoDigests $HERE, not $DIG" ;; esac
case "$THERE" in *"@$DIG"*) ;; *) die "worker: $REF has RepoDigests $THERE, not $DIG" ;; esac
echo "[mc] same registry digest on both Sparks: $DIG"
docker tag "$REF" "$IMAGE"
worker 1 docker tag "$REF" "$IMAGE"
A=$(image_ident "$IMAGE")
B=$(worker_image_ident 1 "$IMAGE")
[ "$A" != missing ] && [ "$A" = "$B" ] || die "head and worker hold different $IMAGE content ($A vs $B)"
echo "[mc] same image content on both Sparks"
./scripts/prepare.sh
)
notes: LICENCE - NON-COMMERCIAL USE ONLY (CC BY-NC-ND drafter): the default drafter incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2 is licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, so this recipe as shipped may only be used non-commercially. Licence-free alternative: DRAFTER=mtp uses the checkpoint's own MTP head instead - no extra licence, ~5-10% slower decode and only ONE request at a time. The drafter is the recipe's DRAFTER line in env_map (one-line change); after changing it, run the install again (it downloads only what is missing) and restart. Two DGX Sparks serve GLM-5.3 Flash (EXL3 4 bpw routed experts) with TensorFold tensor parallelism over the Sparks' RoCE link: 1,048,576-token window per request, up to 4 requests at once, served name GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3 (the same name as the vLLM recipe, so agents keep working). MC talks to the head only; start.sh starts rank 1 on the worker itself over SSH (container glm53-flash-tf on both boxes) and stop.sh removes both. PREREQUISITES: 2x GB10 with 128 GB; the two Sparks cabled over QSFP with RoCE v2 and addresses on one subnet (set the worker's fabric address on its box in MC, else its SSH address is used); key-based SSH login from the head to the worker (the user MC knows for the worker box); Docker with the NVIDIA runtime, your user in the docker group, and rsync on both; ~205 GB free on each box. INSTALL (hours, once): MC writes WORKER/FABRIC_PEER/PORT/PREPARE/DRAFTER into the recipe's .env on the head, checks out the pinned commit, pulls the published image by digest on both boxes and compares the registry digest (RepoDigests) and then the image content (upstream's image_ident - not the local image ID, which differs between containerd and classic image stores), then runs the recipe's prepare.sh: checkpoint Mia-AiLab/GLM-5.3-Flash-EXL3-4bpw-TensorFold (~176 GB, pinned revision) and drafter download on the head, rsync to the worker. START: ./start.sh with PREPARE=0 (the install prepares, a start only starts); first start compiles kernels (~5 min), later starts take 2-6 min; ready when GET /v1/models answers on port 8000. Needs ~110 GiB MemAvailable on each box at start: MC stops other exclusive models on BOTH boxes first. MC does not drop the page cache for this recipe (drop_page_cache=false): TensorFold counts reclaimable cache as available memory. Not validated on a GB10 by MC yet (gb10_validated=false). Pinned to upstream v1.10 (commit 549fdc562c47). Also answers Anthropic's /v1/messages on the same port.
